```{r setup-2, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}

# ── Gompertz-Hilfsfunktionen (direkt aus paper.Rmd übernommen) ───────────────
gomp <- function(t, A, k, t0) {
  A * exp(-exp(-k * (t - t0)))
}

B_AG_max3   <- function(t) gomp(t, A = 100, k = 0.32, t0 = 4.0)
h_stem_f    <- function(t) gomp(t, A = 1.0,  k = 0.40, t0 = 4.0)
h_branch_f  <- function(t) gomp(t, A = 0.7,  k = 0.25, t0 = 3.0)
h_rest_f    <- function(t) gomp(t, A = 0.1,  k = 0.30, t0 = 2.0)

f_stem_g   <- function(t) { hs=h_stem_f(t); hb=h_branch_f(t); hr=h_rest_f(t); hs/(hs+hb+hr) }
f_branch_g <- function(t) { hs=h_stem_f(t); hb=h_branch_f(t); hr=h_rest_f(t); hb/(hs+hb+hr) }
f_rest_g   <- function(t) { hs=h_stem_f(t); hb=h_branch_f(t); hr=h_rest_f(t); hr/(hs+hb+hr) }

#load("../Modell/afs_workspace.RData")

source("../Modell/extract_result.R")

# drop small Biogas plants --> compute total demand and drop all consumer with D<2

## Economics of Agrofoerstry systems

## Agroforestry System Types

.col-50[
**Short-rotation coppice (SRC)**

- Monoculture, 8,000–20,000 cuttings/ha
- Rotation: 3–7 years, stand lifetime: 20–25 years
- Root system regenerates after harvest — no replanting
- Benchmark for biomass production

**Short-rotation AFS (SRAFS)**

- SRC-type tree strips in alley-cropping arrangement
- Trees cover 10–30 % of parcel area
- Boundary effect: higher light & water → higher individual-tree biomass
]

.col-50[
**Long-rotation AFS (LRAFS)**

- Same spatial structure as SRAFS
- Rotation cycles: 12–15+ years
- Larger stem diameter → high-value timber (veneer, sawlogs, engineered wood)
- Timber-quality species: walnut, cherry, oak, high-grade poplar

.callout-note[
**Key insight:** SRAFS and LRAFS are not sharply separated —
**intended use, establishment decisions, and harvest timing** jointly determine economic viability.
]
]

---

## Biomass Growth Models

**Gompertz growth function** für die oberirdische Biomasse $B_{AG}(t)$:

$$B_{AG}(t) = A \cdot \exp\!\bigl(-\exp(-k(t - t_0))\bigr)$$

Komponentenspezifische Anteile (Stamm $p=1$, Äste $p=2$, Reste $p=3$):

$$B_{AG,p}(t) = B_{AG}(t) \cdot \frac{h_p(t)}{h_1(t)+h_2(t)+h_3(t)}$$

- Parameter kalibriert aus SRAFS-Feldversuchen in Süddeutschland `r Citep(bib, "Huber2018_SRAFS_growth")`
- Altersabhängige Ertragskoeffizienten $\eta_{p,a}$ vorberechnet und in das MILP integriert (Restriktion C3)

---

## Gompertz Growth Curves — Poplar Max 3

.col-50[
```{r max3-growth, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=6, out.width="100%"}

ages <- seq(0, 13, by = 0.1)

comp_long <- tibble(
  age       = ages,
  Stem      = f_stem_g(ages)   * B_AG_max3(ages),
  Branches  = f_branch_g(ages) * B_AG_max3(ages),
  Residues  = f_rest_g(ages)   * B_AG_max3(ages)
) |>
  pivot_longer(-age, names_to = "component", values_to = "biomass") |>
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = c("Residues", "Branches", "Stem")))

.col-50[
**Key observations:**

- Stem share rises from ~55 % at age 4 to >75 % at age 10
- Growth peak (inflection) at ~age 4
- Total AGB at age 10: ~65 t dry matter/ha
- Component fractions $f_p(t)$ determine $\eta_{p,a}$ in constraint C3

*Grey band:* typical rotation window (5–10 years)

`r Citep(bib, "Jha2018_Poplar_AFS_Biomass")` — empirical reference points
]

---

## Biomass Supply Chain Literature

| Aspect | State of the art | This paper |
|---|---|---|
| Biomass availability | Exogenous or simplified | Endogenous via Gompertz + age-lag |
| Rotation decisions | Not modelled | Binary $z_{ist}$ with min/max age |
| Product types | Single or aggregated | Multi-product cascade $(p', p) \in \mathcal{Q}$ |
| Network structure | Static | Multi-period, storage + processing |
| Case study scope | Generic | Real SRC sites, Saxony-Anhalt |

.small[Reviews: `r Citep(bib, c("Zahraee2020_BSC_review","Sharma2013_BSC_review"))` &nbsp;|&nbsp; OPTIMASS framework: `r Citep(bib, c("DeMeyer2015_OPTIMASS","DeMeyer2016_tOPTIMASS"))`]

# MILP Model (AFS-SCD)

---

## Sets, Indices & Parameters

.col-50[
**Sets & indices**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | AFS sites (field parcels) |
| $\mathcal{J}$ | Storage/processing facilities |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Industrial consumers |
| $\mathcal{P}$ | Biomass product types |
| $\mathcal{Q}$ | Quality cascade pairs $(p', p)$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Planning periods |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Feasible activity arcs $(s, t)$ |
]

.col-50[
**Key parameters**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\eta_{p,a}$ | Yield (t/ha) for product $p$ at age $a$ |
| $\text{AREA}_i$ | Site area (ha) |
| $c^{est}_i$ | Establishment cost (€/ha) |
| $c^{harv}_i$ | Harvest cost (€/ha) |
| $c^{opp}_i$ | Opportunity cost (€/ha/yr) |
| $R_{kp}$ | Revenue (€/t) at consumer $k$ |
| $d_{ij}, d_{jk}$ | Transport distances (km) |
]

---

## Yield Coefficients $\eta_{p,a}$ — Visualisation

```{r component-fractions, fig.height=3.8, fig.width=10, out.width="98%"}

p1 <- ggplot(shares, aes(x = age, y = share, colour = component)) +

           fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +

           size = 2.6, colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Stem" = "#1b9e77",
                                  "Branches" = "#d95f02",
                                  "Residues" = "#7570b3")) +

  labs(x = "Stand age (years)",

eta_tbl <- tibble(

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("P1 – Stamm" = "#1b9e77",
                                "P2 – Äste"  = "#d95f02",
                                "P3 – Reste" = "#7570b3")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:15) +
  labs(x = "Rotationsalter a (Jahre)",
       y = expression(eta[pa]*" (t TM/ha)"),
       fill = NULL,
       title = expression(paste("Ertragskoeffizienten ", eta[pa], " für MILP-Restriktion C3"))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

p1 + p2
```

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $z_{ist} \in \{0,1\}$ | Binary | Activity arc: site $i$ from period $s$ to $t$ |
| $X_{ijpt} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Biomass flow: site $i$ → storage $j$, product $p$, period $t$ |
| $X_{jkp'pt} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Processed flow: storage $j$ → consumer $k$, cascade $(p',p)$ |
| $S_{jpt} \geq 0$ | Continuous | Inventory at storage $j$, product $p$, end of period $t$ |

.callout-note[
**Age-lag structure:** Arc $(s,t) \in \mathcal{S}^{harv}$ is only feasible if $A_{min} \leq t-s \leq A_{max}$,
enforcing rotation age bounds without additional constraints.
]

---

## Objective Function

**Maximise total contribution margin** over the planning horizon $\mathcal{T}$:

$$\max\; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{k,p} R_{kp} \sum_{j,(p',p),t} X_{jkp'pt}}_{\text{Revenue}} - \underbrace{C^{est} - C^{opp} - C^{main} - C^{harv}}_{\text{Site costs}} - \underbrace{C^{tr\text{-}raw} + C^{tr\text{-}pre}}_{\text{Transport costs}} - \underbrace{C^{stor}}_{\text{Storage costs}}$$

- **Opportunity costs** penalise foregone crop revenues for each year a site is under AFS
- **Two-stage transport** distinguishes raw biomass (site → storage) from pre-treated biomass (storage → consumer)
- **Storage costs** apply from year 2 onward (year-of-harvest drying is cost-free)

---

## Constraints (C1–C4)

**(C1) Single establishment per site:**
$$\sum_{(0,t)\in\mathcal{S}^{est}} z_{i0t} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\; i \in \mathcal{I}$$

**(C2) Path connectivity — flow conservation:**
$$\sum_{(s,t)\in\mathcal{S}} z_{ist} = \sum_{(t,u)\in\mathcal{S}} z_{itu} \qquad \forall\; i,\; t$$

**(C3) Biomass yield via Gompertz coefficients:**
$$\sum_{j} X_{ijpt} \leq \sum_{(s,t)\in\mathcal{S}^{harv}} \eta_{p(t-s)} \cdot \text{AREA}_i \cdot z_{ist} \qquad \forall\; i,p,t$$

**(C4)/(C5) Transport linkage & inventory balance** — follows OPTIMASS network-flow structure `r Citep(bib, "DeMeyer2015_OPTIMASS")`

---

## Constraints (C6–C8) & Cascade Logic

**(C6) Storage capacity:**
$$\sum_{p} S_{jpt} \leq \text{CAP}^{stor}_j \qquad \forall\; j,\; t$$

**(C7) Processing capacity:**
$$\sum_{i,p} X_{ijpt} \leq \text{CAP}^{proc}_j \qquad \forall\; j,\; t$$

**(C8) Demand with quality cascade:**
$$\sum_{j,(p',p)\in\mathcal{Q}} X_{jkp'pt} \leq D^{max}_{kpt} \qquad \forall\; k,p,t$$

.callout-note[
**Product cascade principle:** $(p',p) \in \mathcal{Q}$ allows a **higher-quality product** $p'$ (stems) to satisfy demand for a **lower-quality product** $p$ (chips for energy) — operationalising cascading use as the central economic rationale.
]

---

# Case Study

---

## Study Region & Supply Chain Configuration

- **Region:** tri-state area of Saxony-Anhalt, northern Thuringia, northern Saxony (Germany)
- Highest density of registered SRC *Feldblöcke* in Germany
- **Supply chain structure:** AFS sites → storage/processing nodes → industrial consumers

.col-50[
**Sites $\mathcal{I}$**

- Registered SRC parcels from INVEKOS land-use register
- Clustered into representative site groups
- Site-specific area, establishment/harvest costs
]

.col-50[
**Consumers $\mathcal{K}$**

- 3 biomass product types: stems (P1), branches (P2), residues (P3)
- Industrial consumers: paper/pulp, chemical biorefinery, energy plants
- Minimum demand threshold: $\geq$ 1.5 units/period
]


---

.col-50[

    colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(min(n_clusters, 12), "Set3"))(n_clusters)
  } else {
    scales::viridis_pal(option = "turbo")(n_clusters)
  },
  levels(cluster_assig$hac_cluster)
)

# ── Site polygons: join cluster assignment, project ───────────────────────────
sites_sf_clust <- sites_sf %>%
  mutate(site_id = seq_len(nrow(sites_sf))) %>%
  left_join(cluster_assig, by = "site_id") %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

# ── Consumers & storages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
consumers_plt <- consumers %>%
  mutate(
    total_demand = demand_P1 + demand_P2 + demand_P3,
    kategorie = case_when(
      demand_P1 >= demand_P2 & demand_P1 >= demand_P3 & demand_P1 > 0 ~ "Chemical / Pulp (P1)",
      demand_P2 >= demand_P1 & demand_P2 >= demand_P3 & demand_P2 > 0 ~ "Pulp / Paper (P2)",
      demand_P3 > 0                                                     ~ "Energy / Biogas (P3)",
      TRUE                                                              ~ "Other"
    ),
    pt_size = pmin(4.5, pmax(1.5, 1.5 + log1p(total_demand) * 0.55))
  )

storages_plt <- storages %>%
  mutate(
    #subtype = if_else(type == "Hub", "Logistics Hub", "Sawmill"),
    subtype = if_else(type == "Hub", "Hub", "Hub"),
    pt_size = 3.5
  )

stor_sf <- st_as_sf(storages_plt, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

cons_sf <- st_as_sf(consumers_plt, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

# ── Plot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot() +

  # Base map
  geom_sf(data = de_states,
          fill = "grey96", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_sf(data = rivers_eu,
          colour = "#4292c6", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.7) +

  # KUP site polygons coloured by cluster — legend suppressed via guide = "none"
  geom_sf(data      = sites_sf_clust,
          aes(fill  = hac_cluster),
          colour    = "grey30",
          linewidth = 0.05,
          alpha     = 0.65,
          show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = cluster_pal,
    guide  = "none"          # colours visible on map; no legend entry printed
  ) +

  # Pre-treatment facilities — new colour + shape scale after cluster fill
  ggnewscale::new_scale_colour() +
  ggnewscale::new_scale("shape") +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_sf(data = stor_sf,
          aes(colour = subtype, shape = subtype, size = pt_size),
          stroke = 1.2, alpha = 0.92, show.legend = F) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name   = "Pre-treatment",
    values = c("Sawmill" = COL_SAW, "Hub" = COL_HUB)
  ) +
  # scale_shape_manual(
  #   name   = "Pre-treatment",
  #   values = c("Sawmill" = 16, "Logistics Hub" = 17)
  # ) +

  # Consumer sites — fill scale registered after new_scale_fill() above
  geom_sf(data  = cons_sf,
          aes(fill = kategorie, size = pt_size),
          shape = 22, colour = "white", stroke = 0.45,
          alpha = 0.88, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Consumer type",
    values = c(
      "Chemical / Pulp (P1)" = COL_P1,
      "Pulp / Paper (P2)"    = COL_P2,
      "Energy / Biogas (P3)" = COL_P3,
      "Other"                = "grey60"
    )
  ) +

  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 5), guide = "none") +
  guides(
    fill   = guide_legend(order = 1,
                          override.aes = list(size = 3.5, stroke = 0.4,
                                              colour = "white")),
    colour = guide_legend(order = 2,
                          override.aes = list(size = 4, stroke = 1.5)),
    shape  = guide_legend(order = 2,
                          override.aes = list(size = 4, stroke = 1.5))
  ) +

  coord_sf(
    xlim   = c(bbox_num["xmin"], bbox_num["xmax"]),
    ylim   = c(bbox_num["ymin"], bbox_num["ymax"]),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.25),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.40, "cm"),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title    = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 7)
  )

## MILP Model Parameters

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Planning horizon $\vert\mathcal{T}\vert$ | 40 periods | — |
| Max. rotation age $A_{max}$ | 15 years | LRAFS benchmark |
| Min. rotation age $A_{min}$ | 3 years | SRAFS minimum |
| Raw biomass transport $c^{tr\text{-}raw}$ | 0.08 €/(tkm) | Literature |
| Pre-treated transport $c^{tr\text{-}pre}$ | 0.06 €/(tkm) | Literature |
| Establishment cost $c^{est}$ | 2,500 €/ha | `r Citep(bib, "Testa2014_Poplar_Economics")` |
| Harvest cost $c^{harv}$ | 150 €/ha | Literature |
| Opportunity cost $c^{opp}$ | 45 €/ha/yr | `r Citep(bib, "Faasch2012_SRC_Economics")` |
| Solver | Gurobi 10, MIP gap 1 % | — |

## Yield Sensitivity by Rotation Age

```{r yield-sensitivity, fig.height=3.8, fig.width=10, out.width="98%"}
ages_int <- 3:15

yield_df <- tibble(
  age         = ages_int,
  total_yield = B_AG_max3(ages_int),
  stem_yield  = f_stem_g(ages_int)   * B_AG_max3(ages_int),
  branch_yield= f_branch_g(ages_int) * B_AG_max3(ages_int),
  rest_yield  = f_rest_g(ages_int)   * B_AG_max3(ages_int),
  stem_share  = f_stem_g(ages_int) * 100
)

p_stack <- yield_df |>
  select(age, P1 = stem_yield, P2 = branch_yield, P3 = rest_yield) |>
  pivot_longer(-age, names_to = "product", values_to = "yield") |>
  mutate(product = factor(product, levels = c("P3","P2","P1")))

p_bar <- ggplot(p_stack, aes(x = age, y = yield, fill = product)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values  = c("P1" = "#1b9e77", "P2" = "#d95f02", "P3" = "#7570b3"),
    labels  = c("P1 – Stamm", "P2 – Äste", "P3 – Reste"),
    guide   = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 3:15) +
  labs(x = "Rotationsalter a (Jahre)",
       y = "Ertrag (t TM/ha)",
       fill = NULL,
       title = "Ertragsstruktur nach Rotationsalter") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

p_share <- ggplot(yield_df, aes(x = age, y = stem_share)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1b9e77", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(colour = "#1b9e77", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(55, 75), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 14.7, y = 56.2, label = "55 % (Alter 4)", size = 2.5,
           colour = "grey40", hjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 14.7, y = 76.2, label = "75 % (Alter 10)", size = 2.5,
           colour = "grey40", hjust = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 3:15) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, " %")) +
  labs(x = "Rotationsalter a (Jahre)",
       y = "Stammanteil f₁(a)",
       title = "Stammanteil steigt mit Bestandsalter") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_bar + p_share

# Optimization Results

---

*Key findings from the case study (Saxony-Anhalt):*

- **Active storage nodes:** selected nodes with high accessibility to both SRC clusters and industrial consumers
- **Dominant rotation length:** 5–8 years — balances stem share and harvest frequency
- **Product cascade in use:** P1-stem flows partially satisfy P2/P3 demand at Mercer Stendal (pulp) and UPM Biochemicals Leuna (chemicals)

crs_map <- 25833

# ── Colour palette constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
COL_SAW       <- "#e65c00"

COL_P2        <- "#08519c"

COL_SITE_NONE <- "#bdbdbd"

pal_products <- c(
  p1 = "#1b9e77",  # stem

  p3 = "#7570b3"   # residues
)

# ── Map extent: define once in WGS84, transform to plotting CRS ──────────────
bbox_wgs84 <- st_as_sfc(
  st_bbox(c(xmin = 10.6, xmax = 13.2, ymin = 50.9, ymax = 52.8), crs = st_crs(4326))
)
bbox_map   <- st_transform(bbox_wgs84, crs_map)
bbox_num   <- st_bbox(bbox_map)

# ── Base-map layers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
de_states <- ne_states(country = "Germany", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  st_transform(crs_map) %>%
  st_intersection(bbox_map)

rivers_eu <- ne_download(
  scale = 10,
  type = "rivers_lake_centerlines",
  category = "physical",
  returnclass = "sf"
) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map) %>%
  st_intersection(bbox_map)

# ── Aggregate harvest volumes per site over all periods ──────────────────────
site_harvest <- ext$Xij %>%
  group_by(site_id, product) %>%
  summarise(vol = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from   = product,
    values_from  = vol,
    values_fill  = 0,
    names_prefix = "p"
  )

for (col in c("p1", "p2", "p3")) {
  if (!col %in% names(site_harvest)) site_harvest[[col]] <- 0
}

site_harvest <- site_harvest %>%
  mutate(total_vol = p1 + p2 + p3) %>%
  filter(total_vol > 0)

active_site_ids <- unique(site_harvest$site_id)

# ── Site polygons for background activity map ────────────────────────────────
sites_sf_map <- sites_sf %>%
  mutate(site_id = seq_len(nrow(sites_sf))) %>%
  inner_join( afs_workspace$site_cluster_assig, "site_id" ) %>% 
  st_transform(crs_map) %>%
  mutate(
    active     = hac_cluster %in% active_site_ids,
    site_class = if_else(active, "Active site", "Inactive site")
  )

# ── Pie-chart data: use centroid coordinates in projected CRS ────────────────
sites_pie_sf <- milp_instance$sites %>%
  inner_join(site_harvest, by = "site_id") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

coords_sites <- st_coordinates(sites_pie_sf)

sites_pie <- sites_pie_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(
    x = coords_sites[, 1],
    y = coords_sites[, 2]
  )

vol_med <- median(sites_pie$total_vol[sites_pie$total_vol > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
if (is.na(vol_med) || vol_med <= 0) vol_med <- 1

# radius in map units (metres); tuned for this regional extent
sites_pie <- sites_pie %>%
  mutate(r = 3500 * sqrt(total_vol / vol_med))

# ── Consumers & storages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
consumers_plt <- consumers %>%
  mutate(
    total_demand = demand_P1 + demand_P2 + demand_P3,
    kategorie = case_when(
      demand_P1 >= demand_P2 & demand_P1 >= demand_P3 & demand_P1 > 0 ~ "Chemical / Pulp (P1)",
      demand_P2 >= demand_P1 & demand_P2 >= demand_P3 & demand_P2 > 0 ~ "Pulp / Paper (P2)",
      demand_P3 > 0 ~ "Energy / Biogas (P3)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    pt_size = pmin(4.5, pmax(1.5, 1.5 + log1p(total_demand) * 0.55))
  )

storages_plt <- storages %>%
  mutate(
    subtype = if_else(type == "Hub", "Logistics Hub", "Sawmill"),
    pt_size = pmin(3.5, pmax(1.2, 1.2 + log1p(CAP_proc) * 0.38))
  )

stor_sf <- st_as_sf(storages_plt, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

cons_sf <- st_as_sf(consumers_plt, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_map)

# ── Plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot() +
  # Base map
  geom_sf(data = de_states,
          fill = "grey96", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_sf(data = rivers_eu,
          colour = "#4292c6", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.7) +

  # Site polygons
  geom_sf(data = sites_sf_map,
          aes(fill = site_class),
          colour = NA, alpha = 0.55, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "AFS site status",
    values = c("Active site" = COL_SITE_ACT, "Inactive site" = COL_SITE_NONE)
  ) +

  # Pre-treatment facilities
  ggnewscale::new_scale_colour() +
  ggnewscale::new_scale("shape") +
  geom_sf(data = stor_sf,
          aes(colour = subtype, shape = subtype, size = pt_size),
          stroke = 1.0, alpha = 0.92, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(

  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(

  ) +

- **Price scenarios:** impact of biomass price trajectories (P1/P2/P3) on product mix and supply chain configuration
- **Policy incentives:** effect of AFS subsidies and carbon pricing on establishment decisions
- **Scalability:** solution quality and computation time for larger site/consumer instances

## Harvest quantities


```{r fig-results-harvest-gantt, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Total production quantity of biomass types and its industrial usage over planning horizon (in tons).", fig.width=8, fig.height=4, out.width="90%"}


# ── Labels & colours ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Source side (axis 1): biomass fractions delivered from sites → hubs (Xij)
#   product index 1 = Stems, 2 = Branches, 3 = Residues  [§2.2, f_p(t)]
SRC_LABEL <- c(
  "1" = "Stems",
  "2" = "Branches",
  "3" = "Residues"
)

# Delivery side (axis 2): consumer categories receiving from hubs (Xjk)
#   del_product 1 = Industrial (P1), 2 = Pulp & Paper (P2), 3 = Energy (P3)
DEL_LABEL <- c(
  "1" = "Industrial",
  "2" = "Pulp & Paper",
  "3" = "Energy"
)

# Fill colours for source strata — must match paper Fig. max3-growth
P_COLS_SRC <- c(
  "Stems"    = "#1b9e77",
  "Branches" = "#d95f02",
  "Residues" = "#7570b3"   
)

# ── Aggregate Xjk: src_product × del_product, summed over all periods/consumers
flow_df <- ext$Xjk %>%
  group_by(src_product, del_product) %>%
  summarise(volume = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(volume > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    # axis1 = biomass fraction (source side)
    src = factor(SRC_LABEL[as.character(src_product)], levels = SRC_LABEL),
    # axis2 = consumer category (delivery/sink side)
    del = factor(DEL_LABEL[as.character(del_product)], levels = DEL_LABEL)
  )

# ── Plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot(flow_df,
       aes(axis1 = src, axis2 = del, y = volume, fill = src)) +

  geom_alluvium(
    alpha      = 0.72,
    width      = 1 / 3,
    knot.pos   = 0.45,
    curve_type = "sigmoid"
  ) +

  geom_stratum(
    width     = 1 / 3,
    fill      = "grey94",
    colour    = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  geom_text(
    stat       = "stratum",
    aes(label  = after_stat(stratum)),
    size       = 2.8,
    colour     = "grey15",
    lineheight = 0.88
  ) +

  # Axis header annotations — placed below the stratum columns
  # x = 1 (axis1 = Feedstock fraction), x = 2 (axis2 = End use)
  annotate("text",
    x        = c(1, 2),
    y        = -Inf,
    label    = c("Feedstock", "End use"),
    vjust    = 1.6,
    size     = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour   = "grey30"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Biomass fraction",
    values = P_COLS_SRC          # only 3 source entries; no ghost colours
  ) +

  # ggalluvial uses integer axis positions (1, 2, …); do NOT set
  # limits = c("src", "del") — that breaks stratum positioning
  scale_x_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.25, 0.25))  # widen margins for stratum labels
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    name   = "Volume (t dry matter)",
    labels = comma_format(big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",")
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +   # needed for below-axis annotations
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    axis.title.x       = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x       = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    legend.key.size    = unit(0.42, "cm"),
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 6, r = 6, b = 28, l = 6)
  )
```

```{r fig-results-product-mix, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,     fig.cap="Total biomass delivered to consumers by product type over the planning horizon. Stacked areas show period-level volumes of stem (P1), branches (P2), and residues (P3) flowing from storage hubs to all consumers. Dashed line: total harvested raw biomass shipped from sites to hubs.",  fig.width=8, fig.height=4, out.width="90%"}

shipped_ts <- ext$Xij %>%
  group_by(period) %>%

  geom_area(position = "stack", alpha = 0.80, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +

           y = max(shipped_ts$shipped) * 0.95,
           label = "Raw shipped\n(site→hub)", size = 2.5,
           colour = "#636363", hjust = 1) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Conclusion

---

## Contributions & Key Findings

**Novel MILP formulation (AFS-SCD):** explicit age-lag constraints link establishment and consecutive harvest decisions — first integrated AFS supply chain model of this type

**Allometric Gompertz yield functions** embedded directly in the MILP via pre-computed $\eta_{p,a}$ coefficients — no exogenous biomass input needed

**Multi-product cascade** operationalises cleaner production principle: high-quality material use before energy recovery

**Real-world case study** (Saxony-Anhalt) demonstrates feasibility at regional scale

---

## Open Research Questions

.callout-important[
**Planned computational experiments**
- **Allometric parameter uncertainty:** sensitivity of optimal rotation length to Gompertz parameter ranges
- **Price scenarios:** impact of biomass price trajectories (P1/P2/P3) on product mix and supply chain configuration
- **Policy incentives:** effect of AFS subsidies and carbon pricing on establishment decisions
- **Scalability:** solution quality and computation time for larger site/consumer instances
]

--

**Further directions:**
- Stochastic programming extensions for yield and demand uncertainty
- Multi-objective optimization (economic vs. ecological performance)
- Integration of ecosystem service valuations (carbon sequestration, biodiversity)
